title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: people data with source-system access controls
summary: Hold: Microsoft has not stated the new ACL control's default or how existing people connections will migrate, so the assurances that nothing changes without administrator action and that rebuilding is required are premature. The controls also omit a documented deletion API and stop the permissions path before its setting.

claims.quote: This release enables organizations to bring people data from external systems into Microsoft 365 along with associated access control lists (ACLs)

claims.claim: The planned capability makes Copilot respect permissions defined in source systems.
claims.quote: ensuring Copilot respects existing permissions defined in source systems.

claims.claim: Imported people data can be scoped to specific individuals and groups.
claims.quote: The imported data can be scoped to specific individuals and groups

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Copilot reasoning over people data while honouring access restrictions.
claims.quote: allowing Copilot to reason over people data while honoring access restrictions.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: No feature-specific UI, PowerShell command or API configuration for differentiated people-data ACLs was documented at the time of writing.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Custom people connectors are built using Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.
claims.quote: You build Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data in the same way that you build other Copilot connectors, by using the Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.

claims.claim: A people-data connection must set contentCategory to people.
claims.quote: Copilot connectors that contain people data must have the value people in the contentCategory property of the externalConnections API.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Today's connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.
claims.quote: This connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Uploaded people attributes are stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: When you upload people data, each user's data attributes are scoped to their Microsoft 365 user profile and stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The new ACL control is admin-opt-in and nothing changes on arrival if administrators do nothing.
claims.quote: Searched: "people" "connectors" "access control" "default". Read the roadmap, graph/peopleconnectors and the people-data build guide; none states the new control's default.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to unknown. Replace 'If nobody acts, nothing changes on arrival' with 'Microsoft has not stated the new ACL control's default or whether existing connections change automatically.' Admin configuration of today's connectors does not establish the new control's default.

claims.claim: A connector built under today's rules will keep its everyone ACL after the new capability arrives.
claims.quote: Searched: "people" "connectors" "existing" "ACL" update migration. Read the roadmap, graph/peopleconnectors, the people-data build guide and manage-access-permissions; none describes migration or the resulting ACLs of existing people connections.
claims.fix: Replace the assurance about existing ACLs with 'Microsoft has not documented how existing people connections with everyone ACLs will migrate; verify their permissions when rollout documentation is published.'

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The general connector access-permissions page says changing connection access permissions after creation is not supported.
claims.quote: Updating access permissions after you create the connection isn't currently supported.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The general delete-and-recreate permission workflow establishes how people connectors must move to the planned ACL capability.
claims.quote: Searched: "people" "connectors" "existing" "ACL" update migration. Opened manage-access-permissions and the people-data build guide; neither documents this feature's migration workflow.
claims.fix: Keep deletion and recreation explicitly labelled as today's general connector guidance, not the documented migration route for future people ACLs. Replace 'Plan to rebuild rather than edit' and the categorical At rollout instruction with advice to confirm the published migration process before deleting or rebuilding people connections.

claims.claim: Accounts not matched by their supplied user identifiers are ignored.

claims.claim: The recorded path to a connector's permission model is Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections.
claims.quote: Select the connector you want to review to open the details pane. ... Under Permissions, you can view the permissions set for the connector.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].ui.path to 'Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Permissions' and update the rendered row. The listed path stops at the connections list, omitting both selection and the Permissions section, not just an item-selection step.

claims.claim: No automation counterpart is documented for the general connector-details Permissions view or its connection-level permission-mode selection.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot people connectors Permissions Copilot Visibility Microsoft Graph API update access permissions. Opened manage-access-permissions and the externalConnection resource reference; neither exposes the connector-details Permissions view or permission-mode field through an API.

claims.claim: The general partner-connector visibility toggle is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connection > Copilot Visibility.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. ... Select the connection that you want to modify. ... Under Copilot Visibility, select the toggle to turn the connector on or off, and choose Save.

claims.claim: No API counterpart to the Copilot Visibility toggle is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Visibility" "API" "permissions" connector. Opened manage-connector and the externalConnection resource reference; neither gives an automation equivalent for that toggle.

claims.claim: The pages read do not document admin UI creation of custom people-data connectors.
claims.quote: Searched: custom people data connector create connection admin center people contentCategory. Opened graph/peopleconnectors, the people-data build guide and manage-connector; custom creation uses Graph, while prebuilt people connectors have a separate admin gallery route.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections creates the external connection used for people data.
claims.quote: Create a new externalConnection object. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections

claims.claim: A people connector can be deleted in the Microsoft 365 admin center through Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Delete.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center and navigate to the connectors section. ... On the Your Connections tab, select the connector you want to delete. ... Select the Delete option.

claims.claim: An API for removing the people connector is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Deletes an externalConnection object. ... DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosohr
claims.fix: Populate controls[4].api with kind 'graph', call 'DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/{connectionId}', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/externalconnectors-externalconnection-delete'. People connections use this externalConnection resource; retain the note about deletion delays and do not imply immediate profile-data purging.

claims.claim: Deleting a people connector removes it from all instances, but delays can occur.
claims.quote: If a connector is deleted, it's removed from all instances, but delays can be expected.

claims.claim: The Your Connections list displays a Connection state column.
claims.quote: You can view the connection state for your deployed connectors on the Your Connections tab in the admin center. The state shows in the Connection state column.

claims.claim: Permanent connector crawl failures generate service health notifications.
claims.quote: If a permanent failure occurs, the connection is marked as Failed, and notifications are sent to the service health dashboard under the Issues section for your organization to act on.

claims.claim: The cited general Permissions-view documentation does not specifically confirm coverage of people connectors.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot people connectors Permissions Copilot Visibility Microsoft Graph API update access permissions. Opened manage-access-permissions and the two people-data guides; no text specifically confirms the Permissions pane for people connectors.

claims.claim: The Copilot Visibility documentation describes partner connectors, not confirmed people-connector applicability.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Visibility" "API" "permissions" connector. Opened manage-connector and graph/peopleconnectors; the toggle is documented for partner data sources, without people-specific confirmation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated ACL profile cards Org Explorer information barriers deny identity groups. Opened graph/peopleconnectors and the people-data build guide; no differentiated people ACL identity types, deny support or cross-experience enforcement is specified.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist names profile-property editing and connection monitoring controls without corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Review user editing ... in the SharePoint admin center' and 'Watch the Connection state ... and the service health notifications'. The table covers ACL scoping, Permissions, Copilot Visibility, creation and deletion only.
claims.fix: Add documented rows for profile-property user editing and connection monitoring, or remove those control-specific checklist instructions. Use the existing peopleconnectors citation for editing and manage-connector citation for Connection state and service health; read the linked editing instructions before adding an exact editing path.
